title: "Mini Retirements"
excerpt: "Like a vacation, but much longer. Like a Sabbatical, but smaller."
content_html:
Like a vacation, but much longer. Like a Sabbatical, but smaller. You can do it after finishing school, after switching to a new position or job, or to squeeze in 1-3 months where you do nothing or something for yourself.

I also like Austin Kleon’s way in Steal like an artist Trilogy (Austin Kleon) where he says:

Do Sabbaticals. If you can’t do a long one, do daily, weekly, and monthly. Disconnect, go away from your work, and come back.

Smaller sabbaticals is Walk Everyday, go into Nature. It can be a form of turning off, taking a mini-break.

# Ideas come from Rest

My best decisions and inspirations all came from so-called «mini-retirements». Slowing Down, taking mini retirements, and following the Pathless Path, or just going with the flow. This is the way to go, to find yourself, to listen to your body, your Subconscious. Understanding your body and your inner feelings.

When you do that, you usually get great insights and outcomes from it. But you only learn later, as Steve Jobs said that Connecting The Dots can only be done backward:

Connecting The Dots

Steve Jobs said that a while ago at his commencement speech:
You can’t connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backward. So, you have to trust that the dots will somehow connect in your future.

Isn’t it just a vacation? (Question from HN, thanks!)

To me, vacations are too short to turn off completely. Here, where I live, we have 5 weeks a year, if you are lucky, you can take three in a row in summer. But having two months or more, it’s completely different. Your mind will take time to turn off, to shut down from everyday life, and that’s when the benefit of new ideas comes, usually out of the blue, not forced just because your mind and body are resting from work and everything else.

# My First Three Month Sabbatical

I wrote in Finding My Pathless Path, that while working as an apprentice, I had the advantage of earning a small salary, most of which I saved. This allowed me to take some time off after the apprenticeship to discover the world outside Switzerland. As a curious mind always exploring new things, I wanted to do some traveling.

Back then, it was more like: I wanted to travel and have some fun time off school. From a friend’s recommendation, I chose a language school in Cairns, Australia, and set out for 15 weeks. Seven of which I spent in Cairns and attended school to learn English, and eight I spent traveling the beautiful east coast of Australia.

Reflecting, this trip also shaped me to be who I became. I learned entirely new cultures and environments, and was on my own. In the Pathless Path, Paul calls it mini-retirement; instead of waiting for your retirement in the sixties, take more minor ones along the way.

I still remember to this day how scared I was when I landed in Cairns. It was my first flight and my first time overseas, and I was on the other side of the world. I was lost and numb with no family or friends and not knowing the language and culture well. I didn’t take the easy path with choosing a host family. Instead, I shared flats with unknown people, which made it challenging.

As an introvert, making friends in a foreign language and with many strangers was difficult. Luckily the first day of language school, that changed as I met many other students in the same situation. But seven weeks later, when starting the eight weeks of traveling on my own, the same fear I had came back.

Through these challenges, I got to know myself better. I learned to get out of my comfort zone, appreciate friends and family back home, and how to be open to any feelings or situations that might arise.

These challenging experiences are the ones I remember to this day. In these “stress” situations, you get to know yourself and deeply engage with the surroundings and people around you. It also led to long-time friendships and a genuine appreciation for Australia and a culture other than my own. It also helped that Australia has some of the most beautiful beaches in the world :).

# Others
  • 37Signals, where every X years you get one on top of vacations.
  • Stefan Sagmeister said everything came from his one year off, writing deeper thoughts in his Journaling. Said in How I Write (Podcast).

# Further Reads
  • Sabbaticals keep our attrition at bay by DHH
  • The book The Pathless Path: Imagining a New Story For Work and Life by Paul Millerd | Goodreads

  • Stefan Sagmeister talks about taking 5 years of your retirement and interspersing them into your working years in this great talk, pertinent moments in The power of time off (thanks for sharing HN)

  • Other call it “pre-tirement” in Leave of Absence

Origin: The Pathless Path (Paul Millerd)
References: The 4-Hour Workweek (Tim Ferriss)

content_html_zh:
就像假期一样，但时间更长。 就像休假一样，但规模较小。 你可以在完成学业后，在换了新的职位或工作后，或者挤出一到三个月的时间，什么也不做，或者为自己做点什么。

我也喜欢奥斯汀·克莱恩（Austin Kleon）在《像艺术家一样偷窃》三部曲（Austin Kleon）中的方式，他说：

休假。 如果你不能做很长时间的事情，那就每天、每周、每月都做一次。 断开连接，离开工作，然后回来。

较小的休假是每天散步，走进大自然。 它可以是一种关闭、短暂休息的形式。

# 想法来自休息

我最好的决定和灵感都来自所谓的“迷你退休”。 放慢脚步，短暂退休，走无路可走，或者只是随波逐流。 这就是找到你自己、倾听你的身体、你的潜意识的方法。 了解您的身体和内心感受。

当你这样做时，你通常会从中获得很好的见解和成果。 但你只能在后来才知道，正如史蒂夫·乔布斯所说，连接点只能向后完成：

连接点 史蒂夫·乔布斯不久前在毕业典礼演讲中说过：你无法展望未来，将点点滴滴连接起来；你只能向后看才能将它们联系起来。 所以，你必须相信这些点点滴滴会在你的未来以某种方式连接起来。
不就是一个假期吗？ （HN的问题，谢谢！） 对我来说，假期太短，无法完全休息。 在我住的地方，我们每年有5个星期的假期，如果幸运的话，夏天可以连续参加3个星期。 但两个月或更长时间，情况就完全不同了。 你的思维需要一段时间才能关闭，远离日常生活，这时新想法的好处就会到来，通常是出乎意料的，而不是仅仅因为你的思想和身体从工作和其他事情中得到休息而被迫。

# 我的前三个月休假

我在《寻找我的无路可走》中写道，当学徒时，我的优势是工资微薄，大部分都是我存起来的。 这让我在学徒期结束后可以抽出一些时间去探索瑞士以外的世界。 作为一个总是探索新事物的好奇心，我想做一些旅行。

那时，我的想法更像是：我想去旅行，享受放学后的快乐时光。 在朋友的推荐下，我选择了澳大利亚凯恩斯的一所语言学校，并开始了15周的学习。 其中七年我在凯恩斯度过并上学学习英语，八年我在美丽的澳大利亚东海岸旅行。

回想起来，这次旅行也塑造了我成为现在的我。 我学习了全新的文化和环境，并且只能靠自己。 在《无路可走的道路》中，保罗称之为“迷你退休”。与其等到六十年代退休，不如一路上多做些小事。

直到今天我仍然记得当我降落在凯恩斯时我是多么害怕。 这是我的第一次飞行，也是我第一次出国，而我却在世界的另一边。 我迷失了方向，麻木了，没有家人或朋友，也不太了解当地的语言和文化。 我在选择寄宿家庭时并没有走捷径。 相反，我与陌生人合住公寓，这让我的生活变得充满挑战。

作为一个内向的人，用外语和许多陌生人交朋友是很困难的。 幸运的是，在语言学校的第一天，情况发生了变化，因为我遇到了许多处于同样情况的其他学生。 但七周后，当我开始独自旅行八周时，同样的恐惧又回来了。

通过这些挑战，我更加了解自己。 我学会了走出自己的舒适区，感谢家乡的朋友和家人，以及如何对可能出现的任何感受或情况持开放态度。

这些充满挑战的经历至今仍让我记忆犹新。 在这些“压力”情况下，您会了解自己并深入了解周围的环境和周围的人。 它还带来了长期的友谊以及对澳大利亚和我自己以外的文化的真诚欣赏。 澳大利亚拥有世界上一些最美丽的海滩也有帮助:)。
